    Department of Computer Science
    Data Mining And Machine Learning
    CS (WL) 37300
    WL Fall 2026

    Course Description

    Credit Hours: 3.00. This course will introduce students to the field of data mining and machine learning, which sits at the interface between statistics and computer science. Data mining and machine learning focuses on developing algorithms to automatically discover patterns and learn models of large datasets. This course introduces students to the process and main techniques in data mining and machine learning, including exploratory data analysis, predictive modeling, descriptive modeling, and evaluation.

    Prerequisites: Undergraduate level, CS 18200, Minimum Grade of C and (Undergraduate level, CS 25100, Minimum Grade of C or Undergraduate level, CS 25300, Minimum Grade of C) and (Undergraduate level, STAT 35000, Minimum Grade of C [may be taken concurrently] or Undergraduate level, STAT 35500, Minimum Grade of C [may be taken concurrently] or Undergraduate level, STAT 51100, Minimum Grade of C [may be taken concurrently])

    Course Learning Outcomes

    By the end of the course, you will be able to:

    1. Identify key elements of data mining and machine learning algorithms.
    2. Understand how algorithmic elements interact to impact performance.
    3. Understand how to choose algorithms for different analysis tasks.
    4. Analyze data in both an exploratory and targeted manner.
    5. Implement and apply basic algorithms for supervised and unsupervised learning.
    6. Accurately evaluate the performance of algorithms, as well as formulate and test hypotheses.


    Learning Resources, Technology & Texts

    • No textbooks required

    Assignments

    Exams

    This course will have two in-class midterm exams and one comprehensive final exam. If doing so improves your grade, your lowest midterm score will be replaced with your average exam score (across both midterms and the final). For example, if you earn 30% on Midterm 1, 60% on Midterm 2, and 90% on the Final, your Midterm 1 score of 30% will be replaced with 60%.

    Homework Assignments

    This course will have two kinds of homework assignments: programming assignments and theoretical assignments. Assignments are not equally weighted; theoretical assignments will generally be worth more than programming assignments. Assignments should be submitted via Gradescope.

    Participation Activities

    In-class activities will usually be graded based on completion. A few online Brightspace quizzes (to be completed outside of class) will also count toward your participation grade. Online quizzes are graded for correctness but can be retaken until you earn full points. The three lowest grade items in this category will be dropped.

    Grading Scale

    Per the Purdue University Academic Regulations, the following grades shall be available to be assigned by the instructors and reported when they are called for by the registrar:

    A+ 

    A: Highest passing grade.

    A-

    B+

    B

    B-

    C+

    C

    C-

    D+

    D

    D-: Lowest passing grade; marginally passing minimal objectives of the course.

    E: Conditional failure; failure to achieve minimum objectives, but only to such limited extent that credit can be obtained by examination or otherwise without repeating the entire course. This grade represents failure in the course unless and until the record is duly changed within one semester. It cannot be improved to a grade higher than D. (See section E.) When an instructor reports a grade of E, they shall file in the departmental office a statement of what is required of the student to receive the passing grade.

    F: Failure; failure to achieve minimal objectives of the course. 

    The student must repeat the course satisfactorily in order to establish credit in it.
